#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(sf, tidyverse, tmap, scales)
tmap_mode("plot")
r <- read_rds("data/rds/th3_results.rds")
n <- r$numbers
fmt <- function(x, d = 0) scales::comma(x, accuracy = 10^-d)
pct <- function(x, d = 0) scales::percent(x, accuracy = 10^-d)

## [01 · Research question]{.kicker}Will the new stations be busy, or the next Hume?

::: question
Can a probabilistic spatial interaction model, calibrated on observed tap-ins, forecast ridership at the **29 new JRL and CRL1 stations**, and show which **existing stations lose riders** to them?
:::

::: {.grid .g-4}
::: {.card .accent .stat}
[36]{.num}
[JRL (24) and CRL Phase 1 (12) stations, opening 2028–2030]{.lbl}
:::

::: {.card .accent .stat}
[29 + 7]{.num}
[genuinely new stations + existing stations upgraded to interchanges]{.lbl}
:::

::: {.card .accent .stat}
[`r fmt(sum(r$calibrated$observed_am_tapin) / 1e6, 1)`M]{.num}
[weekday morning-peak tap-ins (May 2022) used to calibrate the model]{.lbl}
:::

::: {.card .accent .stat}
[164 × 286]{.num}
[stations × resident subzones in the choice model]{.lbl}
:::
:::

::: band
**Why it matters.** Hume station stood finished but closed for a decade, and Buangkok and Woodleigh stayed shut when the NEL opened, because expected ridership could not cover operating costs. Planners need station-level forecasts *before* the trains run.
:::

::: {.rows}
::: card
[Inputs]{.ct}

- LTA **OD train flows** (May 2022), **bus stops**, **station exits**
- **Census 2020** population; **HDB** footprints; **OSM POIs**
- URA **MP2025 stations**, **MP2019 land use**; JRL/CRL1 list
:::

::: {.card .soft .tight}
[Data traps found and cleared]{.ct}

- 5 stations **missing X/Y**; Rochor's lat/long ~480 m off its exits
- 3 non-operational codes, incl. **Bukit Brown, a real ghost station**
- URA layer suggests **`r n$naive_new` "new" stations**; only 29 are
- LTA shapefiles with **no EPSG code** (custom "SVY21")
:::
:::
:::

## [03 · Analytical approach]{.kicker}From tap-ins to a station-choice model

::: pipeline
::: step
[1]{.no}
[Clean & build]{.tt}
[Audit five data sources; build origin, destination and two spatial interaction data frames.]{.dd}
[→ 286 origins × 164 / 193 stations]{.out}
:::

::: step
[2]{.no}
[Attraction specs]{.tt}
[Six Huff specifications compared: lines, LRT, closeness, HDB within 800 m, bus stops within 400 m.]{.dd}
[→ Model 4: lines + LRT + HDB 800 m]{.out}
:::

::: step
[3]{.no}
[Huff calibration]{.tt}
[Residents choose a station by its lines, LRT status and surrounding housing, and by access distance; two benchmarks.]{.dd}
[→ R² `r r2f(n$r2)`, CV R² `r r2f(n$cv_r2)`]{.out}
:::

::: step
[4]{.no}
[2030 scenario]{.tt}
[Add 29 stations, upgrade 7 interchanges; re-run with `MCI::huff.shares()`; Tengah build-out test.]{.dd}
[→ forecasts & market areas]{.out}
:::

::: step
[5]{.no}
[Value-added]{.tt}
[**MCI destination-choice model** (second `MCI` model) for alightings; LISA on Huff residuals.]{.dd}
[→ destination demand, regional bias]{.out}
:::
:::

::: chips
[**Demand** · weekday 06:00–09:59 tap-ins]{.chip}
[**Attraction** · lines γ = `r round(n$gamma, 2)`, LRT δ = `r round(n$delta, 2)`, HDB 800 m θ = `r round(n$theta, 2)`]{.chip}
[**Decay** · exponential λ = `r round(n$lambda, 2)` per km]{.chip}
[**Calibration** · optim() on RMSE, 5-fold CV]{.chip}
[**Model 6 check** · + bus stops: CV R² `r sprintf('%.3f', r$cv46[['cv_r2_6']])` vs `r sprintf('%.3f', r$cv46[['cv_r2_4']])`, rank ρ = `r sprintf('%.2f', r$cv46[['rho_46']])`]{.chip}
[**Software** · R: sf, MCI, igraph, spdep, tmap, leaflet]{.chip}
:::

::: band
**Key modelling choice.** Attractiveness depends on the **HDB housing within 800 m** (Model 4), not just on lines and LRT status. Older stations were built inside existing HDB towns; many newer ones sit in districts with little housing yet. Without this term, the model would rate a station in an empty district like one in a mature estate.
:::

## [04 · Key findings]{.kicker}Finding 1: The model reproduces where Singapore boards

::: {.grid .center-v style="grid-template-columns: 1.1fr 1fr;"}
::: figure
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| out-height: 600px
ggplot(r$calibrated, aes(pred_base / n$weekdays, observed_am_tapin / n$weekdays)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = lrt), size = 2.4, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#0b7a83", `TRUE` = "#97c616"),
                      labels = c("MRT", "LRT only"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma()) + scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Predicted AM-peak tap-ins per weekday", y = "Observed") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) + theme(legend.position = c(0.15, 0.88))
```
:::

::: rows
::: {.card .accent .stat}
[`r r2f(n$r2)`]{.num}
[**R²** for 164 stations, vs `r r2f(n$r2_r0)` for nearest-station allocation and `r r2f(n$r2_r1)` for the default Huff model]{.lbl}
:::

::: {.card .accent .stat}
[`r r2f(n$cv_r2)`]{.num}
[**out-of-sample R²** (5-fold cross-validation): parameters are stable, not over-fitted]{.lbl}
:::

::: {.card .accent .stat}
[−`r pct(1 - exp(-n$lambda / 2))`]{.num}
[**attractiveness per extra 500 m** of access distance: residents choose the station they can walk to]{.lbl}
:::
:::
:::

## [04 · Key findings]{.kicker}Finding 2: Count both ends of the trip, not just boardings

::: {.grid style="grid-template-columns: 1.3fr 1fr;"}
::: figure
```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6.6
#| out-height: 660px
r$new_use %>%
  mutate(stn = fct_reorder(str_to_title(stn_name), total_day)) %>%
  select(stn, line, `Boardings (Huff)` = board_day, `Alightings (MCI)` = alight_day) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(stn, line), names_to = "end", values_to = "per_day") %>%
  mutate(end = factor(end, levels = c("Alightings (MCI)", "Boardings (Huff)"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(per_day, stn, fill = end)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = n$p25_use, linetype = 2) +
  annotate("text", x = n$p25_use + 120, y = 2.5, hjust = 0, size = 3.5,
           label = "lower quartile of\nexisting stations") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Boardings (Huff)" = "#0b7a83", "Alightings (MCI)" = "#97c616")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Predicted AM-peak use per weekday (Census 2020 population)", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(legend.position = c(0.78, 0.12))
```
:::

::: rows
::: {.card .teal}
[Strongest new stations]{.ct}

**`r str_c(str_to_title(top_new$stn_name), collapse = ", ")`**, inserted into mature HDB estates beyond walking distance of MRT today, would rank in the **top quarter** of existing stations.
:::

::: {.card .accent}
[Value-added: MCI destination model]{.ct}

On boardings alone, **`r n$n_low`** stations look like ghosts. An MCI model of where passengers *alight* (job and education floor space, network distance) finds **`r n$n_dest` destination stations** and rescues **`r str_c(str_to_title(n$rescued), collapse = ", ")`**.
:::

::: band
**Genuine opening-day risks:** `r str_c(str_to_title(n$still_low), collapse = ", ")`: redeveloping industrial land, NTU campus and airport logistics.
:::
:::
:::

## [04 · Key findings]{.kicker}Finding 3: Tengah's stations depend on housing, not rails

::: {.grid .center-v style="grid-template-columns: 1.2fr 1fr;"}
::: figure
```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5.4
#| out-height: 580px
r$tengah %>%
  pivot_longer(c(census_2020, tengah_buildout), names_to = "scenario", values_to = "per_day") %>%
  mutate(scenario = recode(scenario, census_2020 = "Census 2020 population",
                           tengah_buildout = "Tengah build-out (~130k residents)")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(per_day, fct_reorder(str_to_title(stn_name), per_day), fill = scenario)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.75) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = n$p25 / n$weekdays, linetype = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey70", "#0b7a83")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Predicted AM-peak tap-ins per weekday", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
:::

::: rows
```{r}
#| include: false
tg <- r$tengah %>% filter(stn_code == "JS3"); tp <- r$tengah %>% filter(stn_code == "JE1")
```

::: {.card .accent .stat}
[`r fmt(tg$census_2020)` → `r fmt(tg$tengah_buildout)`]{.num}
[**Tengah (JS3)** morning tap-ins per weekday, from 2020 population to full build-out (42,000 homes)]{.lbl}
:::

::: {.card .accent .stat}
[×`r round(tp$tengah_buildout / tp$census_2020, 1)`]{.num}
[**Tengah Plantation (JE1)**, which becomes one of the JRL's busiest stations]{.lbl}
:::

::: band
**The Hume lesson in numbers.** Whether a JRL station is a white elephant depends on **when homes are occupied relative to opening day**. The model can set a completion threshold for opening each station.
:::
:::
:::

## [04 · Key findings]{.kicker}Finding 4: Losses are local, and upgrades do not guarantee growth

::: {.grid style="grid-template-columns: 1.35fr 1fr;"}
::: figure
```{r}
#| fig-width: 6.6
#| fig-height: 4.3
#| fig-dpi: 220
#| out-width: 100%
base_map +
  tm_shape(r$net_new) + tm_lines(col = "#0b7a83", lwd = 1.3, col_alpha = 0.6) +
  tm_shape(r$impact_sf %>% filter(abs(change_pct) >= 0.05)) +
  tm_symbols(fill = "change_pct", size = 0.7, col = "grey30", lwd = 0.4,
             fill.scale = tm_scale_intervals(style = "fixed",
                                             breaks = c(-1, -0.3, -0.15, -0.05, 0.05, 0.3, 2),
                                             values = "brewer.rd_bu",
                                             labels = c("< -30%", "-30 to -15%", "-15 to -5%",
                                                        "±5%", "5 to 30%", "> 30%")),
             fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Change in AM tap-ins")) +
  tm_shape(r$new_stations) + tm_dots(fill = "#97c616", size = 0.2) +
  map_layout + tm_layout(legend.position = c("right", "bottom"))
```

::: cap
Existing stations changing by 5% or more once JRL and CRL1 open (Census 2020 population)
:::
:::

::: rows
::: {.card .accent .stat}
[`r pct(n$share_div)`]{.num}
[of morning boardings move to the new stations; **`r n$n_loss15`** existing stations lose 15% or more, in three clusters next to the new lines]{.lbl}
:::

::: {.card .teal}
[Hardest hit]{.ct}

Western EWL: **Pioneer, Lakeside, Chinese Garden, Joo Koon** lose over half their boardings to Gek Poh, Jurong West and Tawas.
:::

::: {.card .soft}
[The interchange paradox]{.ct}

`r str_c(str_to_title(upg$stn_name[upg$change_pct > 0]), collapse = ", ")` gain; **`r str_c(str_to_title(upg$stn_name[upg$change_pct < 0]), collapse = ", ")`** lose tap-ins despite the extra line, while transfer crowding still rises.
:::
:::
:::

## [04 · Key findings]{.kicker}Finding 5: No housing within walking distance, no riders

::: {.grid .center-v style="grid-template-columns: 1.35fr 1fr;"}
::: figure
```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5.2
#| out-height: 600px
hc <- r$hdb_cmp
ggplot(hc, aes(hdb_ha_800m + 1, per_day, colour = group)) +
  geom_point(data = filter(hc, group == "Existing (observed)"), size = 2, alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_point(data = filter(hc, group != "Existing (observed)"), size = 3.4) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = filter(hc, group != "Existing (observed)", hdb_ha_800m < 5),
                           aes(label = str_to_title(stn_name)), size = 3.6, show.legend = FALSE,
                           seed = 626, max.overlaps = 20) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = n$p25 / n$weekdays, linetype = 2, colour = "grey40") +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Existing (observed)" = "grey60", "New CRL (predicted)" = "#97c616",
                                 "New JRL (predicted)" = "#0b7a83")) +
  labs(x = "HDB footprint within 800 m (ha + 1, log)", y = "AM-peak tap-ins per weekday (log)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
:::

::: rows
::: {.card .accent .stat}
[ρ = `r round(r$rho_hdb, 2)`]{.num}
[between housing within 800 m and morning boardings at **existing** stations: older lines were built inside existing HDB towns]{.lbl}
:::

::: {.card .accent .stat}
[`r length(r$low_hdb_new)` of 29]{.num}
[**new stations have under 5 ha of HDB housing** within 800 m, in industrial estates, at NTU and near the airport]{.lbl}
:::

::: band
These stations are forecast at the **bottom of the network**. Their case rests on workers, students or future housing, and should be made explicitly.
:::
:::
:::

## [05 · Planning implications]{.kicker}Turning forecasts into decisions

```{=html}
<table class="impl" style="font-size:0.56em">
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Evidence</th><th>Recommended response</th><th>Why</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>New stations with almost no housing within 800 m<br><span style="font-weight:400;color:#66747b">`r str_c(str_to_title(head(r$low_hdb_new, 4)), collapse = ", ")` …</span></td><td>Make the non-resident case explicitly, or defer</td><td>Housing within walking distance is what fills a station in the morning.</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Tengah stations below the ghost-risk line on 2020 population<br><span style="font-weight:400;color:#66747b">JS3 Tengah, JE1 Tengah Plantation</span></td><td>Tie opening to housing completion thresholds</td><td>Forecast boardings rise several-fold at build-out; opening day matters more than the line itself.</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Western EWL and Kovan–Serangoon belt lose 15%+<br><span style="font-weight:400;color:#66747b">Pioneer, Lakeside, Chinese Garden, Kovan</span></td><td>Re-draw feeder-bus routes around new market areas</td><td>Avoid bus kilometres that duplicate the new rail catchments.</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Seven upgraded interchanges<br><span style="font-weight:400;color:#66747b">Jurong East, Boon Lay, Hougang, Ang Mo Kio …</span></td><td><b>Public safety:</b> plan platform, stair and transfer-corridor capacity before opening</td><td>Transfers are invisible in tap-ins but rise at every interchange; crowding at peak transfers is the main safety risk.</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Destination stations with low home-based boardings<br><span style="font-weight:400;color:#66747b">Tukang, Enterprise, Nanyang Gateway, Tengah</span></td><td>Appraise on boardings + alightings, not boardings alone</td><td>The MCI model shows workers and students arriving keep most of them above the ghost-risk line.</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Model over-predicts in the east (LISA)<br><span style="font-weight:400;color:#66747b">Pasir Ris East, Tampines North, Loyang</span></td><td>Treat eastern forecasts as upper bounds</td><td>Residuals cluster significantly (Moran's I = `r round(n$moran, 2)`, p = `r signif(n$moran_p, 1)`).</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.band style="margin-top:12px"}
Forecasts are a **comparative screening tool**: they rank stations and locate impacts reliably, while absolute numbers should be refreshed with current population and opening-day service plans.
:::

## [06 · Limitations]{.kicker}What the forecasts can and cannot support

::: {.grid .g-3}
::: {.card .accent}
[Data]{.ct}

- OD flows (May 2022) and population (Census 2020) pre-date the 2028–2030 network.
- Tap-ins miss **transfers** and **non-resident** demand (e.g. cross-border commuters); land use is a proxy for jobs.
- New-station locations are indicative Master Plan footprints.
:::

::: {.card .accent}
[Method]{.ct}

- Fixed trip rate: no **induced demand**; new boardings are diverted from existing stations.
- Attraction uses lines, LRT status and HDB footprint (a proxy for homes); feeder buses and frequency are missing.
- Straight-line access distance, not walking-network distance.
:::

::: {.card .accent}
[Interpretation]{.ct}

- Forecasts are **home-end morning boardings**, not total station use.
- Residuals cluster regionally, so eastern forecasts are likely optimistic.
- Rankings are robust to parameter uncertainty; absolute values are indicative.
:::
:::
